observation_DATO: NFE2L2 0.75x and NQO1 0.73x lower in a KO organoid, NFE2L2 lower in shWWOX neural cells (transcript only, n 4 v 2 and n 1 per arm); NRF2 protein, nuclear NRF2 and target activity are not measured in any WWOX-deficient neural system (INV-08 W01, W02, W08)
relation_INFERENZA: If the response is insufficient (H1), nuclear NRF2 and target-gene activity are lower by genotype and rise on KEAP1-Kelch occupancy; the rise needs NRF2
action_IPOTESI: Occupy the KEAP1 Kelch pocket with a non-covalent binder (no cysteine chemistry) and read target activity and a function endpoint in neurons and astrocytes separately, each with and without a verified NFE2L2 loss
context_cell_and_time: neurons and astrocytes separately, early postnatal-equivalent stage, acute exposure under one fixed oxidant challenge; endpoint time with the knockdown shown adequate at that time
compound_or_class_and_role: KI-696 (CHEMBL3819587): PROBE (structure confirmed; nanomolar in epithelium, 40 uM needed with one enantiomer in LUHMES; brain exposure and neuronal permeability unknown); not a candidate
expected_result: a genotype difference at baseline or after challenge; the compound raises nuclear NRF2 and two target genes in KO more than in control; effect lost under adequate loss; function endpoint follows
counter_evidence: NQO1 and G6PD higher in shWWOX (W02); HMOX1 and SRXN1 higher in organoid and P47T (W01, W05): the transcripts are mixed; no WWOX-system protein datum
possible_harm: Sustained NRF2 activation changes metabolism and redox in ways not studied in this cell (IPOTESI); the one human neuronal use found (Zhu 2025) moved ferroptosis markers in the harmful direction on a KEAP1-overexpressing, NRF2-high background
refuting_experiment: no genotype difference at baseline (axis moves toward inert); no rise of target genes in neurons at any tolerated exposure; effect unchanged under verified NFE2L2 loss (independent route); worsening
class: new combination in the repository (a binder with a documented NRF2-loss arm in glia, applied to the WWOX premise); novelty against the literature not assessed
consumer: INV-08 steps X0-X2 and open question IT45-Q03 (reagent pair now named); compound view V19 name list

observation_DATO: HMOX1, SRXN1 and GSR higher in organoid, Hmox1 and Srxn1 modestly higher in P47T brain (W01, W05); KI696 on KEAP1-overexpressing, NRF2/HO-1-high hiPSC cortical interneurons raised Fe2+, MDA and cytokines and lowered GSH and GPX4 (Zhu 2025, no loss arm)
relation_INFERENZA: If the response is already induced but insufficient (H2) or maladaptive, further KEAP1 disruption adds little or worsens, and the benefit-versus-risk curve across graded occupancy is informative; a single concentration cannot show it
action_IPOTESI: Use the binder as a graded ladder (several on-target response levels, matched by nuclear NRF2 and two target genes) and read a benefit endpoint and a risk panel (GSH, GPX4, lipid peroxidation, cytokines, viability) in the same wells, KO against control
context_cell_and_time: same cultures as NH1; the ladder runs at the endpoint time and again after a second, later exposure
compound_or_class_and_role: KI-696: PROBE for the ladder; bardoxolone methyl (covalent, neurotoxic in LUHMES above nanomolar): conditional COMPARATOR only inside a non-toxic window; fumarate esters: comparator with documented NRF2-independent routes
expected_result: a genotype x occupancy interaction: benefit at low occupancy, none or harm above it in KO; control cells monotone
counter_evidence: a monotone benefit across the ladder in KO cells; a Zhu-like harm in control cells too (then not a genotype effect)
possible_harm: the risk panel moves without a function change (marker without consequence); a Zhu-like change could be caused by the KEAP1 overexpression and not by the binder
refuting_experiment: a monotone benefit across occupancy with an unchanged risk panel in KO
class: new combination (ferroptosis-axis readouts as the risk arm of the NRF2 ladder); novelty not assessed
consumer: INV-08 step X1 (add a risk panel and a graded series); DL-MECH-125 (GPX4); W07 (ferroptosis in a cancer-cell abstract)

observation_DATO: Verified loss of Nrf2 in primary rat microglia removes the induction by the binder (HO1, NQO1, GCLC about 4-8-fold to about 1) and the protection, and KEAP1 loss occludes it (Wu 2024); RA839, another non-covalent binder, regulated 105 probe sets in macrophages and two in Nrf2 knock-out cells (abstract only); a fumarate keeps an HCAR2-dependent route on Tnf, Il1b, Hmox1 and Nr4a2 in a microglial line (Parodi) and modifies 24 other proteins in neurons and astrocytes (abstract)
relation_INFERENZA: The count and identity of genes that a reagent still regulates after verified NRF2 loss measure its NRF2-independent action, which NQO1 alone cannot; for the binder it should be near zero, for a fumarate not
action_IPOTESI: Run the covalent and the non-covalent reagent in the same cell, each at matched on-target response, with a verified NFE2L2 loss arm and a KEAP1-loss occlusion arm, and read a transcript panel or array: the survivors after loss are the independent action
context_cell_and_time: one cell class at a time (neurons, astrocytes, microglia-like cells); same time and medium for both reagents
compound_or_class_and_role: KI-696 (probe) against dimethyl fumarate and monomethyl fumarate (comparators), RA839 (conditional second binder, abstract-level) to show the result is not one chemotype; bardoxolone methyl only if a non-toxic window is shown
expected_result: binder: survivors near zero and occlusion by KEAP1 loss; fumarate: a residual set on inflammatory genes; both lose the target-gene panel under loss
counter_evidence: the binder keeps a residual set under verified loss (its action is not only through NRF2 in that cell); both classes lose everything (no discrimination between them in that cell)
possible_harm: an array or panel survivor count depends on the knockdown adequacy and on the baseline; a floor effect (Wu CCK-8 0.20) can mimic dependence on viability endpoints
refuting_experiment: survivor genes of the binder equal those of the fumarate
class: known-but-unused design (Winkel's array arm, abstract only) applied to a neural cell: new combination; novelty not assessed
consumer: S6 design in INV-08 X2; comparison engine rows C-K1 to C-K3; IT45-Q03

observation_DATO: The neuron-specific Wwox deletion carries the phenotype and glia deletions do not (W09, flat and underpowered); tBHQ-induced neuronal gene change depended on astrocytic Nrf2 in mixed cortical cultures (Kraft 2004, abstract only)
relation_INFERENZA: Whether the benefit of a KEAP1 binder reaches a WWOX-deficient neuron through its own NRF2 or through astrocytic NRF2 (H3) cannot be seen in a mixed culture; cell-type-restricted loss separates the two
action_IPOTESI: Co-cultures in which only the astrocytes, or only the neurons, lack NFE2L2, with the binder against vehicle, reading neuronal network function and viability
context_cell_and_time: neuron-astrocyte co-culture; WWOX-null neurons with NFE2L2-intact or -null astrocytes, and NFE2L2-null neurons with intact astrocytes
compound_or_class_and_role: KI-696 (probe); no compound is needed to read the genetic arms alone (the genetic arm first)
expected_result: benefit lost when astrocytes lack NFE2L2 and kept when neurons do (compartment H3); the reverse (cell-autonomous)
counter_evidence: the neuron deletion data (W09) show astrocytes alone do not produce the phenotype, not that they cannot rescue; the binder has not been used in astrocytes in any source reached
possible_harm: astrocytic NRF2 activation may shift composition or glial reactivity (IPOTESI)
refuting_experiment: loss in either compartment leaves the effect unchanged (compartment does not matter) or no effect in any arm
class: known-but-unused (Kraft abstract) with a binder: new combination; novelty not assessed
consumer: INV-08 step X3; open question IT45-Q03
